lessons.sourceEnglishTitle: Explain the Menú del Día to a Newly Arrived Friend
lessons.sourceEnglishObjective: Explain step by step how a fixed-price lunch works and why, then have your friend explain it back.
lessons.title: 日替わり定食の仕組みを友人に説明する
lessons.objective: Explain how a fixed-price Japanese lunch set works, compare it with individual orders, clarify a surcharge and coffee price, then ask a newly arrived friend to explain it back.
lessons.focus: 日替わり定食 is the day’s set meal. 主菜 is the main dish and 副菜 a side dish. ～が含まれています names included items; 別料金 and 追加料金 mark separate and extra charges. 最初に…それから…最後に… sequences an explanation.
lessons.scene: Emma takes newly arrived Lucas to a home-style restaurant in Kanazawa and explains the chalkboard lunch set.

cards.ja: 最初に主菜を選んで、それから副菜を選びます。
cards.en: First choose the main dish, then choose a side dish.

cards.ja: ご飯と味噌汁は定食に含まれています。
cards.en: Rice and miso soup are included in the set meal.

cards.ja: 和牛の主菜には三百円の追加料金がかかります。
cards.en: The Wagyu main dish has a three-hundred-yen surcharge.

cards.ja: 黒板を見てから席に座ると分かりやすいです。
cards.en: It helps to read the chalkboard before sitting down.

cards.ja: すみません。コーヒーは定食に含まれていますか。それとも別料金ですか。
cards.en: Excuse me. Is coffee included in the set meal or charged separately?

cards.ja: 分かりました。コーヒーは別料金ですね。
今度はあなたが説明してみてください。
cards.en: Now try explaining it back to me.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: エマとルーカスは金沢の家庭料理の店に入ります。昼どきで、近くで働くお客さんがたくさんいます。
reader.en: Emma and Lucas enter a home-style restaurant in Kanazawa at lunchtime. Many nearby workers are there.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: ルーカスは日本に来たばかりで、入口の黒板を見ても定食の仕組みが分かりません。
reader.en: Lucas has just arrived in Japan and does not understand the set-meal chalkboard at the entrance.

reader.speaker: Emma
reader.ja: 黒板によると、日替わり定食は千四百円です。単品で頼むよりお得です。
reader.en: According to the board, the daily set meal is fourteen hundred yen, a better value than ordering individual dishes.

reader.speaker: Emma
reader.ja: 最初に主菜を選んで、それから副菜を選びます。
reader.en: First choose the main dish, then choose a side dish.

reader.speaker: Emma
reader.ja: 今日は主菜が焼き魚か鶏の照り焼きで、副菜は煮物かサラダです。
reader.en: Today the main dish is grilled fish or teriyaki chicken, and the side is simmered vegetables or salad.

reader.speaker: Emma
reader.ja: 和牛の主菜もありますが、三百円の追加料金がかかります。
reader.en: There is also a Wagyu main dish, but it has a three-hundred-yen surcharge.

reader.speaker: Lucas
reader.ja: ご飯と味噌汁もその値段に入っていますか。
reader.en: Are rice and miso soup included in that price?

reader.speaker: Emma
reader.ja: はい。ご飯と味噌汁、それに今日のデザートが含まれています。
reader.en: Yes. Rice, miso soup, and today’s dessert are included.

reader.speaker: Emma
reader.ja: 厨房で作る料理を毎日数種類に絞っているので、定食の値段を抑えられるそうです。
reader.en: The kitchen makes only a few dishes each day, which helps keep the set-meal price down.

reader.speaker: Emma
reader.ja: だから、席に座る前に黒板を確かめるといいですよ。
reader.en: That is why checking the board before sitting down helps.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: エマはコーヒーも含まれると思いましたが、店員に確認します。
reader.en: Emma thinks coffee may be included, but checks with the server.

reader.speaker: Emma
reader.ja: すみません。コーヒーは定食に含まれていますか。それとも別料金ですか。
reader.en: Excuse me. Is coffee included in the set meal or charged separately?

reader.speaker: Server
reader.ja: デザートは含まれていますが、コーヒーは別料金です。
reader.en: Dessert is included, but coffee is charged separately.

reader.speaker: Emma
reader.ja: 分かりました。コーヒーは別料金ですね。
reader.en: I understand. Coffee is extra.

reader.speaker: Emma
reader.ja: 今度はあなたが説明してみてください。
reader.en: Now try explaining it back to me.

reader.speaker: Lucas
reader.ja: 最初に主菜と副菜を選びます。ご飯と味噌汁とデザートは含まれています。和牛には追加料金があって、コーヒーは別料金です。
reader.en: First I choose a main and a side. Rice, miso soup, and dessert are included. Wagyu has a surcharge, and coffee is extra.

speaking.role: Friend explaining a fixed-price lunch set to a newcomer
speaking.opening: この黒板の日替わり定食は、どういう仕組みですか。
speaking.goal: Explain the sequence and included items, compare set and individual prices, clarify the surcharge and coffee charge with staff, then ask the friend to explain the arrangement back in Japanese.
speaking.closure: 今度はあなたが説明してみてください。

lessons.sourceEnglishTitle: Why the Kitchen Closes at Four: Explaining Local Rhythm
lessons.sourceEnglishObjective: Explain to a fellow traveler how lunch hours, sobremesa and closures work here, and check your facts with staff.
lessons.title: 昼と夜の営業時間を確かめる
lessons.objective: Explain this restaurant’s lunch, afternoon break, last order, and evening reopening to a fellow traveler, then verify the exact time with staff.
lessons.focus: 昼の営業 and 夜の営業 distinguish lunch and evening service. ラストオーダー is the last kitchen order. 休憩時間 marks the interval between services. 店員に確認しましょう turns an assumption into a checked fact.
lessons.scene: At three thirty, two travelers find a neighborhood restaurant’s kitchen closed and ask the server about reopening.

cards.ja: この店の昼のラストオーダーは二時です。
cards.en: This restaurant’s last lunch order is at two.

cards.ja: 三時半に来ると、厨房は休憩時間です。
cards.en: If you come at three thirty, the kitchen is on its break.

cards.ja: 無視されているわけではありません。昼の営業が終わったんです。
cards.en: They are not ignoring you. Lunch service has ended.

cards.ja: 今すぐ食べたいなら、軽食があるか聞いてみましょう。
cards.en: If you want to eat now, let us ask whether there is a snack.

cards.ja: すみません。夜の厨房は何時から開きますか。
cards.en: Excuse me. What time does the kitchen open for evening service?

cards.ja: 五時半からまた注文できますか。
cards.en: Can we order again starting at five thirty?

cards.ja: 私が時間を勘違いしていました。
それまで近くで軽食を食べましょう。
cards.en: Until then, let us eat a snack nearby.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 午後三時半、フェムケとダニエルは町の食堂に入ります。
reader.en: At three thirty, Femke and Daniel enter a neighborhood restaurant.

reader.speaker: Femke
reader.ja: 定食を頼もうとしたら、厨房はもう閉まったと言われました。
reader.en: I tried to order the set meal, but they told me the kitchen had closed.

reader.speaker: Daniel
reader.ja: 無視されているわけではありません。昼の営業が終わったんです。
reader.en: They are not ignoring you. Lunch service has ended.

reader.speaker: Daniel
reader.ja: 入口の看板では、昼のラストオーダーは二時です。
reader.en: The sign at the entrance says the last lunch order is at two.

reader.speaker: Daniel
reader.ja: 三時半は昼と夜の営業の間の休憩時間なんですね。
reader.en: Three thirty is the break between lunch and evening service here.

reader.speaker: Femke
reader.ja: この辺では、昼食は何時ごろ食べる人が多いですか。
reader.en: Around what time do people here usually eat lunch?

reader.speaker: Daniel
reader.ja: 正午から一時半ごろが多いと思います。でも、この店の時間は店員に確認しましょう。
reader.en: I think many eat between noon and one thirty. Let us check this restaurant’s hours with staff.

reader.speaker: Femke
reader.ja: 食後にコーヒーを飲んで話す人もいますか。
reader.en: Do some people drink coffee and talk after eating?

reader.speaker: Daniel
reader.ja: そういう人もいますが、店ごとの営業時間は違います。
reader.en: Some do, but each restaurant has its own hours.

reader.speaker: Daniel
reader.ja: すみません。夜の厨房は何時から開きますか。
reader.en: Excuse me. What time does the kitchen open for evening service?

reader.speaker: Server
reader.ja: 看板のとおり、五時半からです。
reader.en: As the sign says, from five thirty.

reader.speaker: Daniel
reader.ja: 五時半からまた注文できますか。
reader.en: Can we order again starting at five thirty?

reader.speaker: Server
reader.ja: はい。五時半から夜のメニューを注文できます。
reader.en: Yes. You can order from the evening menu starting at five thirty.

reader.speaker: Daniel
reader.ja: 私が時間を勘違いしていました。教えてくださってありがとうございます。
reader.en: I misunderstood the time. Thank you for explaining it.

reader.speaker: Femke
reader.ja: それまで近くで軽食を食べましょう。
reader.en: Until then, let us eat a snack nearby.

speaking.role: Traveler explaining and checking lunch-service hours
speaking.opening: 厨房が閉まっていると言われました。どうしてですか。
speaking.goal: Explain the posted last-order and break times, discuss after-meal conversation without treating it as a universal custom, ask staff for the exact reopening, correct your earlier assumption, and suggest an interim snack.
speaking.closure: 私が時間を勘違いしていました。教えてくださってありがとうございます。

lessons.sourceEnglishTitle: Coach a Friend Through Ordering at a Busy Taco Stand
lessons.sourceEnglishObjective: Coach a friend with short commands on how to order, add salsas and pay at a crowded stand, then let them do it.
lessons.title: 混んだ屋台で友人に注文を任せる
lessons.objective: Coach a friend through ordering at a busy yakitori stall with short Japanese commands, then let the friend state quantities, choose seasoning, and pay.
lessons.focus: ～を注文して, ～を選んで, and ～を伝えて are short conversational commands. 焼き鳥 is grilled chicken skewers, 本 counts skewers, and たれ／塩 distinguish sauce and salt seasoning. 今度はあなたの番です hands the task to the friend.
lessons.scene: Daniel helps Aiko order at a crowded evening yakitori stall, then steps back so she completes the order.

cards.en: Tell the cook the kinds and quantities.

cards.ja: 七味は少しずつ試して。
cards.en: Try the seven-spice a little at a time.

cards.ja: ももを二本、つくねを一本、たれでお願いします。
cards.en: Two thigh skewers and one meatball skewer with sauce, please.

cards.ja: お会計はいくらですか。
今度はあなたの番です。
食べ終わったら店主に払って。
cards.en: Pay the cook when you finish.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 夜の屋台は混んでいて、ダニエルは友人のアイコと焼き鳥の列に並びます。
reader.en: The evening stall is crowded. Daniel and Aiko line up for yakitori.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 店主はもも、つくね、ねぎまの串を次々に焼いています。
reader.en: The cook grills thigh, meatball, and chicken-and-scallion skewers one after another.

reader.speaker: Daniel
reader.ja: どの串を食べたいか、先に決めて。種類と本数を伝えて。
reader.en: Decide which skewers you want first. Tell him the kinds and quantities.

reader.speaker: Aiko
reader.ja: ももとつくねにします。
reader.en: I will have thigh and meatball skewers.

reader.speaker: Daniel
reader.ja: たれか塩を選んで。
reader.en: Choose sauce or salt.

reader.speaker: Daniel
reader.ja: 七味はここにあります。少しずつ試して。
reader.en: The seven-spice is here. Try it a little at a time.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 店主は列を進めながらアイコに声をかけます。
reader.en: The cook moves the line along and addresses Aiko.

reader.speaker: Cook
reader.ja: 次の方、何本ですか。
reader.en: Next person, how many skewers?

reader.speaker: Daniel
reader.ja: 今度はあなたの番です。
reader.en: Now it is your turn.

reader.speaker: Aiko
reader.ja: ももを二本、つくねを一本、たれでお願いします。
reader.en: Two thigh skewers and one meatball skewer with sauce, please.

reader.speaker: Cook
reader.ja: はい、少々お待ちください。
reader.en: Certainly. Please wait a moment.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 店主が焼き鳥を渡し、アイコは自分で七味を少し加えます。
reader.en: The cook hands over the skewers, and Aiko adds a little seven-spice herself.

reader.speaker: Aiko
reader.ja: お会計はいくらですか。
reader.en: How much do I owe?

reader.speaker: Cook
reader.ja: 九百円です。
reader.en: Nine hundred yen.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: アイコは小銭を出して、自分で支払います。
reader.en: Aiko takes out her coins and pays on her own.

speaking.role: Friend coaching and then yielding a yakitori order
speaking.goal: Use short Japanese commands for skewer kinds, quantities, sauce or salt, and payment; then step back while the friend orders and pays without English.
speaking.closure: 今度はあなたの番です。
